I bought this to replace our LG refrigerator water filter. We use filter # 5231JA2002A. The first time I tried installing it, I didn't get the filter attached in its housing correctly, but I didn't realize it, and woke up to a flooded fridge and a damaged wood kitchen floor. After mopping up, I tried reinstalling. This time I pushed the filter up into its housing much more firmly and it felt like it was installed correctly. (I pressed it upward until I felt a soft click into place, then rotated it into the lock position.) But the filter fell out of its housing again. I had a bowl under it this time so I didn't have a huge flood to dry up, but I was surprised the filter fell this second time. Then my husband installed it -- same process, and he also felt he had the thing in there correctly but it fell out again. I'm returning this. Either it flat-out doesn't fit correctly, or it's so difficult to install the right way that you can't tell if you've got a tight seal or if you're going to face a wet mess. Poor design and/or incorrect labeling for the filter item number.

While this filter does fit the same as a DA29-00003G filter, it does not filter the same. It's akin to a DA29-00003F filter (chlorine taste, and cloudiness) and doe not filter cysts, chemicals, and heavy metals.

Arrived in time and in good shape. Fits well. That's good part, and has little to do with "Refresh" or whoever is behind this product. Now the nasty bits. Literally and figuratively.

It took many, many gallons of flushing to eliminate the creepy-looking little bits of material from my water. This was not the innocuos discoloration from the carbon block that I would see from the Samsung filter.

The one big thing I can't abide is a company that tries to trick consumers into thinking the product is something that it isn't. Starting with the Amazon listing, Refresh wants to appear to be the original Samsung product. "Samsung Aqua-Pure DA29-00003G Water Filter..." That's written to deceive us.

And later, in the Description "...activated carbon block filter which has received NSF42 approval." That, and all references to NSF "approval" on the refreshmywater.com website are flat-out lies. The WQA has certified the Refresh products to certain NSF/ANSI standards for material safety and structural integrity ONLY. Not removal of solids, cysts, chemicals just materials of construction. This product has no independent certification of removal of foreign materials from your drinking water.

But on the Refresh website, they use the NSF logo and they have a whole page that would have us believe that they have received "Our filters are 100% NSF Certifed." Whatever that means!
